title: QuickOps: 15-Min Integrator Roleplay & Battlebrief (v0.2)
summary: A compact, field-friendly roleplay and battlebrief for seller/SEs to run 15-minute integrator conversations that surface constraints, risk signals, and immediate fallbacks. Emphasis on diagnose->demo->safeguard flow and two-minute technical handoffs to platform teams.
content:
Purpose:
- Very short, practical script for SEs and sellers when talking to integrators/platform engineers during a pilot kickoff or discovery call.
- Goal: in 15 minutes surface 3 critical constraints (latency target, data residency, throughput), propose a safe configuration (hosted -> dedicated -> private fallback), and leave a clear next action: scope pilot or schedule technical deep-dive.

Audience:
- Integration engineers, platform owners, SREs, and technical buyers.
- Not for product marketing. Keep it technical, concrete, and ops-oriented.

One-page flow (15 minutes):
1) 0:00-02:00 — Quick framing + credibility
   - "We help teams get predictable inference at scale; this call is to understand one constraint so we can propose a safe pilot. Two quick questions and a config recommendation."
   - Drop proof: "We've run similar pilots at X where we cut per-token cost by 30% while meeting 99th p latency goals." (swap X with relevant customer)

2) 02:00-06:00 — Rapid constraint triage (ask aloud, confirm)
   - Q1: "What is your target end-to-end latency for the user interaction (95th/99th)?"
   - Q2: "Expected concurrent inference QPS (or average requests/min)?"
   - Q3: "Are there hard data residency or compliance controls for request payloads or logs?"
   - Quick note-taking shorthand: LAT=, QPS=, RESID=, KV (key-value cache) allowed? Y/N

3) 06:00-09:00 — Surface workload characteristics
   - Typical prompt length (tokens) or context window size? (short, medium, long)
   - Predictability of traffic (steady, bursty, unpredictable)
   - Need for streaming or function/tool calling? (yes/no)

4) 09:00-12:00 — Immediate safe recommendation (3 configs)
   - If low latency (<150ms) + moderate QPS: recommend hosted with pinned model + prefix caching; explain how prefix caching reduces token cost and tail latency.
   - If high QPS (>200) or predictable throughput: recommend Dedicated reserved pool; note autoscale policies and burst lanes.
   - If data residency or air-gap: recommend Private (VPC) with customer KMS and shorter retention; offer an on-prem proof plan.
   - Format: "Given LAT=__, QPS=__, RESID=__, my recommendation is: ____ (why, quick risk notes, next step)."

5) 12:00-15:00 — Two-minute technical handoff + next steps
   - "If you want the pilot this week we need: a sample 50–200 request trace, a short IAM account or sample VPC peering plan for Private, and 1 engineer for a 45-minute follow-up. I will send a checklist after call."
   - Confirm who owns the follow-up, schedule, and expected decision date.

Risk Signals cheat-sheet (fast scan during call):
- Secret-handling red flags: long unredacted logs, unencrypted keys in requests, no KMS
- Latency/timeouts: client-side 1s timeouts (we need to push to 2s), lots of retries
- Operational limits: strict 99.99% SLA requirement for user-facing inference, cost-capped experiments (<$500/mo)
- Traffic patterns: sustained spikes (holiday/batch) vs short bursts

Fallback & escalation quick-matrix (speak plainly):
- Capacity gap: if Dedicated quota missing -> temporary hosted burst + rate-limit/queueing on client with exponential backoff; submit a capacity fast-track JIRA (JIRA-OPS-827).
- Quality regression on quantized models: fall back to full-precision variant for canary traffic; alert product-oncall and create a regression ticket (CONFLUENCE-12345).
- Compliance block on hosted: escalate to Private presales + Security review (2-week SLA for POC onboarding).

Roleplay scripts (two variants)
- Fast integrator (10-minute, tight):
  SE: "Quick ask — what latency 95th do you need?"
  Integrator: "Under 200ms ideally, but 95th can be 400ms."
  SE: "Got it. Typical prompt sizes?"
  Integrator: "~120 tokens."
  SE: "Ok. With that I recommend hosted pinned model with prefix caching — low friction and we can set a canary at 5% traffic. If it goes well, Reserved Dedicated is next step. I'll send a one-page checklist."

- Deep integrator (15-minute, ops-focused):
  SE: "Do you have an internal NLB or sidecar that will call our API?"
  Integrator: "Yes, internal gateway with 200ms client timeouts and no KMS yet."
  SE: "Two changes: bump timeouts to 1s and we'll collaborate on KMS integration. For pilot: hosted with dedicated canary lane and rate-limit rules to avoid retries. I'll open the capacity fast-track ticket and loop infra."

Quick handoff checklist to send after call (email template in slack thread):
- 1x request trace (50–200 samples)
- sample prompt length distribution (tokens)
- expected QPS and peak concurrency windows
- contact for platform/infra (name + email)
- any compliance docs (DPA, SOC2 point of contact)
- desired pilot dates and success criteria (latency target, cost cap, quality threshold)

One-pager for SE to paste into follow-up (copy/paste friendly):
- "Thanks for the quick sync. Recommendation: [hosted|dedicated|private]. Pilot scope: X days, traffic canary at Y%, success metrics: 95th latency < __ ms, accuracy/regression threshold: __. Next steps: please share traces and infra contact. Owner: [name]."

Common objections + short counters (speak like engineer):
- "We can't send sensitive payloads to hosted." -> "We can limit retention, use envelope encryption, or propose the Private POC; we'll document data flow for your security team."
- "Cost looks high on Dedicated." -> "Start with small Dedicated pool + autoscale; Redwood Optimize suggestions after 2 weeks usually cut unit cost by 15–30%."
- "What if model drifts?" -> "We set up evaluation hooks and regression alerts tied to your sample prompts; immediate fallback to stable variant if regressions appear."

Playbook snippets for SEs to carry in pocket (short bullet cheat):
- Always capture LAT, QPS, RESID in first 4 minutes.
- If LAT goal <200ms, propose streaming + small batch sizes.
- If QPS >200, recommend Dedicated or discuss autoscale/commit.
- If RESID=Strict, ask for KMS ownership and offer Private timeline.

Backchannel actions (after call)
- SE to open JIRA with tags: pilot, customer-accelerator, ops-fasttrack; assign to operations lead.
- Post a concise note in #sales-ops with decision + pilot dates. Attach traces.

Appendix: sample quicknotes templates (to paste into CRM or follow-up)
- Subject: Pilot next steps for [acct] — quick config
- Body: "Recap: LAT=__, QPS=__, Tokens=__. Recommendation: hosted pinned model with 5% canary -> Dedicated on commit. Required artifacts: traces, infra contact. Target pilot start: __. Owner: [SE name | email]."

Open questions / things to iterate in v0.3:
- Add a tiny latency calculator: tokens->avg token time for popular model families.
- Tiny checklist for customers using request-side timeouts under 500ms.
- Short decision tree graphic for sellers (convert to slide).

Notes to self:
- Swap placeholder customer names per region.
- Pair with a one-click calendar invite template and a trace upload form.
- Get input from Priya on compliance phrasing for EU customers.

Document history: v0.1 initial brain-dump (2025-10-20); v0.2 cleaned and added handoff checklist (2025-11-03); last edits and collaborator comments incorporated (2025-12-12).
